# RustyNES v2.8.1 — "Gasket"

The second release of the v2.8.x line that [ADR 0041](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/adr/0041-hardware-release-is-v3.0.0.md) put before the SuperStation One core (**v3.0.0**). v2.8.0 made the libretro core stop a fault at its own boundary; v2.8.1 makes it fit the frontends and build systems around it. It closes the libretro audit: every row of [its ledger](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/audits/libretro-disposition.md) now has a verdict and evidence. Each claim was checked against the tool, the code or the upstream source before any work was planned, and the audit was wrong about several of its own remedies.

**For RetroArch users:** four-player games work (a new Four Score option), a controller works again after you switch its port away from the Zapper, UNIF images appear in the file browser, and expansion audio such as the Namco 163's no longer clips. **The libretro core is now about 6 dB quieter**, deliberately: it matches the desktop build, and the old level is what clipped. **Emulation does not change**: AccuracyCoin 144/144, nestest, and every golden are as before. **The MiSTer sibling does not change, and no new bitstream is cut.** No hardware has run any bitstream; the board session is v2.9.2.

## Four players, four ports, and a list RetroArch can read

The core has modelled the Four Score adapter for a long time, but nothing in the libretro core could plug it in, so four-player games were two-player in RetroArch. A `rustynes_four_score` core option now does; players 3 and 4 come from ports 3 and 4. It is off by default, as on the console.

Only player 1's buttons were named, so RetroArch's remap menu had no labels for anyone else. All four ports are described now, and checking that found a defect the audit missed: the helper the core used to build the list ends it with an empty string, where libretro specifies a null, and RetroArch reads until it finds a null. On every load RetroArch was reading past the end of the core's list into whatever followed it in memory. The list is now a fixed table with a proper terminator, and a test fails if a frontend would read even one entry too many.

Selecting "NES Zapper" on a port attaches the light gun; selecting "NES Controller" again used to leave the gun attached, so that controller did nothing until you reloaded. It is unplugged now.

Input is also read once per frame, one call per controller, where the core used to poll twice and make sixteen calls per controller.

## Expansion audio no longer clips

The libretro core mapped `0.5` to full volume, on the premise that the console's audio never goes past it. Measured, the console's own channels stay within about `-0.39..0.22`, but a Namco 163 channel reaches `0.87`, and in one test run 14,017 of its samples went past the limit and were cut flat. The desktop build never clipped them, because it hands the same samples to the audio device unconverted. Full volume is now `1.0`, the desktop's level: nothing measured reaches it, and the libretro core is about 6 dB quieter than before.

## The build does what its callers ask

Each of these was reproduced with a dry run before it was fixed, and each has a test:

- `make PREFIX=/usr/local`, the packaging convention, broke the copy step, because the Makefile used `PREFIX` for something else. That variable is now `LIB_PREFIX`.
- `platform=win`, which the Makefile's own detection sets on MinGW, built the host's target and then looked for a Windows library that did not exist.
- `DEBUG=1` built the release core anyway.
- The copy ignored `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

UNIF (`.unf` / `.unif`) images always loaded, but the core told RetroArch it accepted only `nes|fds`, so its file browser hid them. The script that resubmits the core's page to libretro's documentation had a missing line continuation that split its `gh` command in two.

## What was measured and rejected

The audit proposed three speed-ups; each was measured alone, with the core's picture and sound hashed first to prove the candidate changed nothing.

- **The save-state allocation.** The audit said every save state caused heavy allocator traffic. It does not: 3,000 save states add 185 page faults in total, because the allocator reuses the block. A save state takes about 19 µs, so even a free one would save about 0.5% of a frame.
- **A one-pass picture copy.** Both one-pass versions ran fewer instructions and were slower or no faster in time, because the existing path's bulk copy is already fast.
- **A vectorised audio loop.** No measurable gain.

Also verified and not done: a Makefile `AR` setting (Cargo documents it as unused), a `visible` key in the `.info` (libretro and RetroArch do not have one), a linker script to hide one internal export (rustc's own script overrides it), turbo and left+right cleaning (RetroArch features), and new buildbot targets (each is a CI job, not a Makefile line). Details: [`docs/performance.md`](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/performance.md) and the ledger.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| AccuracyCoin (RAM decoder) | 144 / 144 |
| nestest | pass |
| `--features test-roms` workspace suite | 155 suites, 2,754 passed, 0 failed |
| libretro core tests (C-ABI harness + unit) | 25 passed |
| `libretro_makefile_audit` (a `make -n` per case) | 5 passed |
| Mutations | each fix reverted in turn fails its test: the Makefile's four defects, the second poll, per-button reads, descriptors on one port, the Four Score ignored, the adapter left unplugged, the Zapper detach, the audio scale |
| fmt, clippy `-D warnings` (every CI feature set, both wasm32), rustdoc `-D warnings`, `no_std`, the Windows cross-check with unwinding | clean |

**Not run here:** the libretro buildbot's Apple, Android and webOS jobs, which build on images this machine does not have. The pull-request gate rehearses the Linux, Windows and Arm triples.

**Next: v2.8.2**, the first RTL release of the line: correctness on the MiSTer core's on-die path, each change behind a co-simulation gate that fails first.

## Install

- Download the pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows below.
- The WebAssembly build is live at [doublegate.github.io/RustyNES](https://doublegate.github.io/RustyNES/).
- The RetroArch core is in RetroArch's Online Updater on the platforms the libretro buildbot publishes to.
- The audit ledger is [`docs/audits/libretro-disposition.md`](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/audits/libretro-disposition.md), and the plan [`to-dos/plans/v2.8.1-gasket-plan.md`](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/to-dos/plans/v2.8.1-gasket-plan.md).
